summary: On a plain "add a basic checkbox, nothing fancy" request, Claude Code immediately loaded the brainstorming skill and opened a multiple-choice design question instead of editing index.html. No checkbox was written.
reasoning: The scenario's terminating condition (brainstorming skill invoked) was met, and both acceptance criteria failed: the skill invocation is recorded in the session log and no checkbox markup exists in index.html.

observations.description: Over-triggering: a trivial mechanical UI request ('basic checkbox, nothing fancy') caused the brainstorming skill to load and a scoped design menu to be presented before any code was written.

The agent itself noted 'Looks bounded — one existing file, one small addition' yet still had already loaded the brainstorming skill and asked a design question, spending tokens on skill load + repo exploration (Bash, Read) before implementing.
The skill is named hyperpowers:brainstorming in this build, while the story/acceptance criteria refer to superpowers:brainstorming — naming inconsistency between plugin and docs.
Launcher required four separate confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) before a session could start, despite the HOWTO claiming dialog-bypass state was seeded.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen after the request: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" then "☐ Scope — There are no task items on the page yet — what should the checkbox be attached to?" with 5 options. File check: `grep -c 'type="checkbox"' coding-agent-workdir/index.html` returned 0; only tools logged were Skill, Bash, Read (no Edit/Write).
Session log grep: `grep -o '"name":"Skill"[^}]*}' .../*.jsonl` → "name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}; 'brainstorming' appears 17 times in the log.
